name: Khobz Bel Zebda w Mrebba (Bread with Butter, Jam or Cheese)
description: The Algerian breakfast tartine: fresh khobz or baguette spread with butter and apricot jam, or topped with a slice of cheese, with a glass of milk coffee or mint tea.

steps.text: Slice the bread and warm it briefly if it is not fresh.
Spread with butter, then jam; or butter then a slice of cheese.

tips: Toast the slices lightly in a dry pan for a crunchier tartine.

name: Sfenj (Algerian Fried Doughnut Rings)
description: Light, chewy, golden ring doughnuts fried in oil, eaten warm with sugar or honey and mint tea.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the water and beat 8 minutes into a very soft, sticky dough.
Cover and rise until doubled and bubbly, about 1 hour.
With wet hands take an egg-sized piece of dough, poke a hole in the middle and stretch into a ring.
Fry in hot oil (about 170 C) 2 minutes per side until golden.
Drain and serve warm with honey or sugar.

tips: Keep your hands wet to handle the sticky dough.

name: Khfaf (Algerian Light Fritters)
description: Airy, golden fritters of a soft yeasted batter dropped by spoonful into hot oil: the quick cousins of sfenj, dusted in sugar.

steps.text: Whisk flour, yeast, sugar, salt and water into a thick smooth batter. Rest 40 minutes.
Drop tablespoons of batter into 170 C oil and fry 2 minutes per side until deep golden.
Drain and roll in sugar.

name: Harcha (Semolina Griddle Cakes)
description: Crumbly, golden semolina rounds cooked on a griddle, split and served hot with butter, honey or cheese.

steps.text: Mix the semolina, sugar, salt and baking powder, rub in the melted butter.
Add milk to form a firm dough, rest 10 minutes.
Shape into 6 discs 1.5 cm thick and dust with semolina.
Cook on a medium dry griddle 6 minutes per side.

name: Yaourt Maison (Homemade Yoghurt)
description: Smooth homemade yoghurt from just milk and a spoon of live yoghurt, set overnight.

steps.text: Heat the milk to just below boiling (85 C), hold 5 minutes, then cool to 42 C.
Whisk the starter with a ladle of milk, stir back in with the milk powder.
Pour into jars, cover and keep warm (oven with light on) for 8 hours.
Chill for 4 hours before eating.

tips: Keep the jars still while they set.

name: Raïb (Home-fermented Milk)
description: Raïb is milk left to turn gently sour at room temperature into a tangy, drinkable, spoonable fermented milk.

ingredients.name: yoghurt
ingredients.note: live, or raïb from the last batch

steps.text: Warm the milk to body temperature (about 37 C).
Stir in the starter, cover and keep in a warm place for 12 hours.
Chill and serve cold, stirring before drinking.

tips: Use raïb from the last batch as the next starter.

name: Lben (Traditional Buttermilk)
description: The tangy buttermilk left when raïb is churned for butter, the drink of every Algerian summer table and the base of many soups.

steps.text: Pour the raïb into a large jar or churn.
Shake or churn for 20 to 30 minutes until specks of butter form.
Add cold water, shake briefly, and lift out the butter; the liquid left is lben.

tips: Serve cold with a pinch of salt and dried mint.
